edges.effect_quant: Different designs and subgroups point in different directions, so a single pooled estimate is not the right way to read this edge.
edges.mechanism: Any fracture benefit from 1000 IU/day would mainly come through correcting mild insufficiency, not from pharmacologic bone effects in already replete adults.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2019 Yao meta analysis in JAMA Netw Open, which suggests that vitamin d about 1000 iu/day produces mixed findings across studies for fractures. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Subgroup differences, dose thresholds, and competing mechanisms likely explain why the literature does not settle into one clean direction.
